name: Prader-Willi-like Syndrome

criteria.description: Neonatal hypotonia with poor suck and feeding difficulties
Development of hyperphagia leading to obesity in early childhood
Mild to moderate intellectual disability or developmental delay
Characteristic facial dysmorphism resembling Prader-Willi syndrome
Endocrine dysfunction including hypogonadism or growth hormone deficiency
Absence of 15q11-q13 deletion or imprinting defects typical of Prader-Willi syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of neonatal hypotonia, hyperphagia with obesity, and cognitive impairment in the absence of typical Prader-Willi syndrome genetic abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of classic Prader-Willi syndrome by genetic testing.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neonatal hypotonia with poor suck reflex
Hyperphagia leading to early childhood obesity
searchTerms: early childhood weight gain from hyperphagia

common.symptomName: Hypogonadism with delayed or incomplete puberty
Short stature due to growth hormone deficiency
searchTerms: short height from growth hormone lack
delayed growth due to hormone deficiency
small stature from low growth hormone

common.symptomName: Characteristic facial dysmorphic features (almond-shaped eyes, narrow forehead)
Behavioral problems including temper tantrums and compulsivity

occasional.symptomName: Sleep-disordered breathing including obstructive sleep apnea

rare.symptomName: Type 2 diabetes mellitus secondary to obesity
searchTerms: high blood sugar due to weight

laboratory: Elevated serum leptin levels consistent with obesity
Hormonal assays showing growth hormone deficiency and hypogonadism
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or nonspecific
Skeletal X-rays may show scoliosis or delayed bone age
genetic: Absence of 15q11-q13 deletion or imprinting defects characteristic of Prader-Willi syndrome
Possible mutations in genes associated with syndromic obesity phenotypes
other: Polysomnography may reveal obstructive sleep apnea

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of 15q11-q13 deletion or imprinting defect
More severe hypotonia and developmental delay
Retinal dystrophy leading to vision loss
Obesity with cognitive impairment but distinct genetic cause

redFlags: Rapid weight gain with hyperphagia in infancy
Severe neonatal hypotonia with feeding difficulties
references: Cassidy SB, Driscoll DJ. Prader-Willi syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2009;17(1):3-13.
Gold JA, et al. Prader-Willi-like syndrome: clinical and molecular characterization. Am J Med Genet A. 2012;158A(4):789-795.
